title: Pool Supplies Giant Files Bankruptcy, Shuttering 76 Stores Nationwide – Fox Business Report
body:
Leslie’s Inc., the nation’s largest retailer of pool and spa supplies, announced on Tuesday that it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The filing is part of a restructuring plan that will see the company shutter 76 of its more than 800 stores and reduce its debt load by roughly $685 million, while keeping the remaining locations fully operational and continuing to serve customers nationwide.

The restructuring agreement was reached with a consortium of Leslie’s existing lenders, who will provide new financing to support the company’s ongoing operations. Under the plan, the retailer will close a mix of underperforming stores across the United States, primarily in markets where sales have lagged behind the industry’s overall rebound. The closures are expected to be completed by the end of the first half of 2025, after which Leslie’s will emerge from bankruptcy with a leaner footprint and a stronger balance sheet.

Industry analysts say the move reflects broader pressures facing specialty retail chains that depend heavily on discretionary spending. While the pool‑and‑spa market has benefited from a post‑pandemic surge in home improvement projects, rising construction costs, supply‑chain disruptions and a tightening credit environment have squeezed margins. Leslie’s, which reported a 12 percent drop in net sales for the fiscal year ending June 30, has been grappling with inventory excesses and higher financing costs. By shedding debt and consolidating its store network, the company aims to improve cash flow and re‑allocate resources toward e‑commerce and service‑driven offerings such as installation, maintenance and repair.

The bankruptcy filing also underscores the challenges of operating a brick‑and‑mortar model in an increasingly digital marketplace. Over the past three years, Leslie’s has invested heavily in its online platform, which now accounts for roughly 30 percent of total sales. However, the company’s physical stores still represent a critical touchpoint for customers who prefer in‑person assistance with product selection, chemical testing, and equipment sizing. By closing underperforming locations, Leslie’s hopes to concentrate foot traffic in its most profitable stores, enhance the in‑store experience, and better integrate online and offline channels.

Creditors appear supportive of the restructuring, noting that the proposed debt reduction will bring the company’s leverage ratio down to a more manageable level. The new financing package includes a $200 million revolving credit facility that will fund working capital needs and support inventory replenishment as the retailer navigates seasonal demand cycles. In addition, the agreement provides for a modest cash‑in‑exchange‑for‑equity infusion from existing lenders, giving them a stake in Leslie’s post‑restructuring future.

Looking ahead, Leslie’s management has outlined a strategic roadmap that emphasizes growth in high‑margin services, expansion of its private‑label product lines, and deeper penetration into emerging markets such as the Sun Belt, where residential pool installations continue to rise. The company also plans to leverage data analytics to fine‑tune inventory assortments and personalize marketing campaigns, aiming to boost customer loyalty and increase average transaction values. If the restructuring proceeds smoothly, Leslie’s could emerge from Chapter 11 within 12 to 18 months, positioned to capitalize on the sustained popularity of home‑based recreation while maintaining a healthier financial foundation.
